newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's army bemoans immoral recruits.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's army bemoans immoral recruits.

text.p: Vietnam's official army newspaper, complaining that military recruits were sometimes ill-educated and immoral, called on Wednesday for a drive to enlist better-quality soldiers.

"Among newcomers, education and morals have been severely limited," the Quan Doi Nhan Dan said in an editorial. "In some localities, young people with a criminal record, illiterates or people suffering from social diseases have been allowed to join the army," it said.
It said such recruits had hampered the training of army units and were responsible for desertion and violation of military regulations.
"The aim in recruiting newcomers this year is to minimize the number of youngsters who do not meet the criteria for joining the army," it said.
Communist Vietnam's army was estimated in 1995 to have a force of 572,000 personnel and a strategic rear force of three to four million.
